newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PM's approval rating moves ahead of rival.
newsitem.headline: Czech PM's approval rating moves ahead of rival.

text.p: Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus has halted a drop in public confidence and his support has moved back above that of his political arch-enemy, Social Democrat Milos Zeman, a survey released on Monday said.

The survey in early January by the independent agency STEM among 1,617 Czechs, showed the approval rating for Klaus, the conservative leader of the ruling Civic Democratic Party (ODS), rose to 49 percent from 46 percent in November.

Klaus's approval had been dropping steadily since its peak of 71 percent in early 1994. Klaus and his party lost its majority in parliament in general elections last June and he was forced to form a minority coalition government.
The opinion poll excludes responses for President Vaclav Havel, who is one of the most popular Czech public figures but is not directly elected.
The opposition Social Democrat (CSSD) leader and parliamentary chairman Zeman fell to a 43 percent approval rating, down from 49 percent.

For the first time in Czech history the most popular politician is a woman. Petra Buzkova, a vice-chairwoman of CSSD and a senior party leader in parliament, rose to 69.5 percent approval from 64 percent in the previous poll.
Buzkova has been on maternity leave from parliament since November and is expected to take her seat when parliament convenes again in early February.

Industry and Trade Minister Vladmir Dlouhy of the ruling coalition party the Civic Democratic Aliance (ODA), who has topped the STEM survey since its inception in 1993, fell into second place although his approval rose to 69 percent from 68.
